q-62834.name: Question 1
q-62834.problem:
The total number of participants $S(t)$ registered for an online conference after $t$ days is given by the function

$$
S(t)=40+{\int }_{0}^{t}(4x-16)\,\text{d}x,
$$

where $t>0$ is the time, in days, since the conference was announced. 

At what time is the number of participants at a minimum, and how many participants are registered at this time?
q-62834.worked_solution:
To find when the number participants is minimized, we need to solve $\frac{\text{d}S}{\text{d}t}=0.$ First, we differentiate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}S}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(40+{\int }_{0}^{t}(4x-16)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(40)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({\int }_{0}^{t}(4x-16)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}{\int }_{0}^{t}(4x-16)\,\text{d}x \\  & =4t-16\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve $\frac{\text{d}S}{\text{d}t}=0$:

$$
4x-16=0\,⟹\,t=4
$$

So there are two candidates for global extrema, $t=0$ and $t=4.$ To find out how many participants are registered when $t=4,$ we figure out $S(4)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}S(4) & =40+{\int }_{0}^{4}(4x-16)\,\text{d}x \\  & =40+{[2{x}^{2}-16x]|}_{0}^{4} \\  & =40+[(2(4)^{2}-16(4))-(0)] \\  & =40-32 \\  & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Since $8<40$, we conclude that the minimum number of participants is $8$, and this occurs after $4$ days.

dSdt=ddt(40+∫0t(4x−16)dx)=ddt(40)+ddt(∫0t(4x−16)dx)=ddt∫0t(4x−16)dx=4t−16

4x−16=0⟹t=4

q-349973.name: Question 2
q-349973.problem:
The rate at which water flows into a tank is given by the function

$$
r(t)=6t+10,
$$

where $r(t)$ is measured in liters per hour and $t>0$ is the time in hours since $1\,\text{p.m}.$
Water is also draining from the tank at a steady rate of $8$ liters per hour.

If there were $200$ liters of water in the tank at $1\,\text{p.m},$ how many liters of water will be there at $5\,\text{p.m}?$

There will be 
{{field-1}}  liters of water in the tank at $5\,\text{p.m}.$
q-349973.worked_solution:
Water is flowing into the tank at a rate of $6t+10$ liters per hour and is draining at a rate of $8$ liters per hour. Therefore, the **rate of change** in the amount of water (call it $R(t)$) is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(t) & =r(t)-8 \\  & =6t+10-8 \\  & =6t+2.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the **total amount of water** after $t$ hours (call it $T(t)$), we apply the second fundamental theorem of calculus:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =T(0)+{\int }_{0}^{t}R(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =200+{\int }_{0}^{t}(6x+2)\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

To ensure that $T$ is a function of $t$ only, we use a different variable ($x$) for the integration. 

To find out the amount of water after $4$ hours ($5\,\text{p.m}$), we substitute $t=4$ into the above and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(4) & =200+{\int }_{0}^{4}(6x+2)\,\text{d}x \\  & =200+(3{x}^{2}+2x){|}_{0}^{4} \\  & =200+[(3\cdot 16+8)-0] \\  & =200+56 \\  & =256\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, there will be $256$ liters of water in the tank at $5\,\text{p.m}.$

q-349984.name: Question 3
q-349984.problem:
A city is tracking the number of bikes available in a bike-share station.
They observe that bikes are returned to the station at a rate $r(t)$ given by the function

$$
r(t)=5{t}^{3}+2t,
$$

where $r(t)$ is measured in bikes per hour, and $t>0$ is the time in hours since tracking began.
At the same time, $4$ bikes are rented from the station each hour.

If there were initially $100$ bikes at the station, find the expression that gives $B(t),$ the number of bikes at the station $t$ hours after tracking began.

$B(t)=\frac{5}{4}{t}^{4}\,+$
{{field-1}}
q-349984.worked_solution:
The number of bikes is increasing at a rate of $r(t)$ bikes per hour and is decreasing at a rate of $4$ bikes per hour. Therefore, the **rate of change** $R(t)$ of the number of bikes is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(t) & =r(t)-4 \\  & =5{t}^{3}+2t-4.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the total number $B(t)$ of bikes after $t$ hours, we apply the second fundamental theorem of calculus:

$$
\begin{aligned}B(t) & =B(0)+{\int }_{0}^{t}R(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =100+{\int }_{0}^{t}(5{x}^{3}+2x-4)\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

To ensure that our final function is a function of $t$ only, we use a different variable ($x$) for the integration.

We can simplify the expression as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}B(t) & =100+{\int }_{0}^{t}5{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{t}2x\,\text{d}x-{\int }_{0}^{t}4\,\text{d}x \\  & =100+{5\,\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}|}_{0}^{t}+{2\,\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}|}_{0}^{t}-4x{|}_{0}^{t} \\  & =100+\frac{5}{4}{t}^{4}+{t}^{2}-4t \\  & =\frac{5}{4}{t}^{4}+\,{t}^{2}-4t+100\end{aligned}
$$

q-349996.name: Question 4
q-349996.problem:
On a certain afternoon, the total number of people $N(t)$ visiting the city's zoo is given by the function

$$
N(t)=60+{\int }_{0}^{t}(48-3{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x,
$$

where $t>0$ is the time (in hours) since noon.  

At what time is the number of people in the zoo at a maximum, and how many people are at the zoo at that time?

The maximum number of people is
{{field-1}}
after
{{field-2}}
hours.
q-349996.worked_solution:
To find when the number of people at the zoo is at maximum, we need to solve $\frac{\text{d}N}{\text{d}t}=0.$ First, we differentiate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}N}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(60+{\int }_{0}^{t}(48-3{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(60)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({\int }_{0}^{t}(48-3{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}{\int }_{0}^{t}(48-3{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =48-3{t}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve $\frac{\text{d}N}{\text{d}t}=0$:

$$
48-3{t}^{2}=0\,⟹\,t=4
$$

So there are two candidates for global extrema, $t=0$ and $t=4.$ To find out how many people are in the zoo when $t=4,$ we figure out $N(4):$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(4) & =60+{\int }_{0}^{4}(48-3{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =60+{[48x-{x}^{3}]|}_{0}^{4} \\  & =60+[(48\cdot 4-{4}^{3})-(0)] \\  & =60+[192-64] \\  & =60+128 \\  & =188\end{aligned}
$$

Since $60<188$, we conclude that the maximum number of people at the zoo is $188$, and this will happen after $4$ hours.
